title: Your First Weekend at Marist University, Shared as Cards
description: A calm, under-21-safe first-weekend route: get oriented, settle into campus, find creative and reflective spaces, then take in the Hudson Valley.

cards.title: Start with a self-guided campus loop
cards.subtitle: First stop · Marist Campus
cards.notes: Open the official campus map, locate the library and Student Center, then use the numbered destinations to make your own first-day walking route.
cards.short_summary: A practical way to put names and buildings together before the weekend fills up.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s official campus map identifies academic buildings, the Murray Student Center, dining halls, Student Activities, and other campus destinations.
cards.access_notes: Use the official map as a navigation aid; observe campus access rules.

cards.title: Choose a library seat with a view
cards.subtitle: Settle-in stop · Campus green and Hudson River side
cards.notes: Pick an individual or group seating area, browse the collections, or use a desktop workstation while you get acquainted with academic support spaces.
cards.short_summary: A three-story academic hub with study seating, collections, technology, and a coffee bar.
cards.evidence_claim: Cannavino Library has seating for individual and group study, physical and online collections, computer access, and academic-support functions.
cards.source_title: James A. Cannavino Library - Marist University
cards.access_notes: Campus building; confirm current building access and service hours before visiting.

cards.title: Find the campus’s gathering point
cards.subtitle: Midday stop · Murray Student Center
cards.notes: Walk through to spot the student lounge, meeting rooms, Student Government office, theatre spaces, dining services, and the campus bookstore for later use.
cards.short_summary: A central building for student services, events, dining, music, and meeting spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Murray Student Center includes meeting rooms, dining services, a student lounge, Student Government, theatre and music spaces, and the campus bookstore.
cards.access_notes: Campus building; individual spaces and events may have separate access arrangements.

cards.title: Pause on the four-acre campus green
cards.subtitle: Afternoon reset · Adjacent to Murray Student Center
cards.notes: Bring a book or meet a new classmate outdoors, then use the nearby Student Center as your next indoor waypoint when you are ready to continue.
cards.short_summary: An open campus lawn beside the Student Center with Hudson River views.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist describes a four-acre campus green adjacent to the Student Center that overlooks the Hudson River.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; follow posted campus rules and weather guidance.

cards.title: Make a first meal plan
cards.subtitle: Dinner stop · North End complex
cards.notes: Check the current dining information, then choose an on-campus meal that fits your plan and dietary needs before heading to an evening activity.
cards.short_summary: One of Marist’s on-campus dining locations in the North End complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist lists North End Dining Hall on its campus map and describes international cuisine among dining offerings in the North End complex.
cards.access_notes: Meals require an applicable dining purchase or plan; verify current menus and hours with Marist Dining.

cards.title: Look for a student theatre night
cards.subtitle: Evening option · Murray Student Center
cards.notes: Check the Marist Theatre calendar or club updates for a production, then arrive with enough time to find the theatre and review any ticket instructions.
cards.short_summary: A named Student Center theatre used by Marist’s theatre community and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: Nelly Goletti Theatre is located in the Murray Student Center, and Marist Theatre produces multiple productions each year.
cards.access_notes: Performance availability and ticketing vary; check the current event listing before going.

cards.entity_name: Our Lady Seat of Wisdom Chapel
cards.title: Take a quiet chapel break
cards.subtitle: Reflection stop · Library-side entrance
cards.notes: Use the daily quiet-prayer hours for a brief, respectful pause; the nearby interfaith prayer room is also accessed from the chapel’s library side.
cards.short_summary: A campus space for prayer, reflection, services, and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist states that Our Lady Seat of Wisdom Chapel is open daily for quiet prayer from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Daily quiet-prayer hours are 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; be respectful of services and other users.

cards.title: Walk the riverfront at Longview Park
cards.subtitle: Saturday daytime · Marist Hudson River waterfront
cards.notes: Follow the bike/walk path, stop at the fishing pier or gazebo, and keep to designated public paths while taking in the Hudson River scenery.
cards.short_summary: A 12-acre Marist riverfront park with a path, pier, gazebo, boathouses, and views.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist describes Longview Park as a 12-acre riverfront park with a bike/walk path, fishing pier, historic Cornell Boathouse, and gazebo.
cards.access_notes: Use designated paths and waterfront areas; conditions and event use can affect access.

cards.title: Spot a piece of Regatta Row history
cards.subtitle: Riverfront detail · Longview Park
cards.notes: View the restored two-story boathouse from the park, then compare it with the adjacent Marist Boathouse while staying outside operational rowing areas.
cards.short_summary: A restored historic boathouse on Marist’s Hudson River campus waterfront.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist identifies the historic Cornell Boathouse as one of two campus boathouses on the Hudson River and says its upper level hosts campus events.
cards.access_notes: View from public park areas; boathouse interiors and events have separate access requirements.

cards.entity_name: Walkway Over the Hudson State Historic Park
cards.title: End with a Hudson crossing
cards.subtitle: Sunday daytime · Poughkeepsie entrance at 61 Parker Avenue
cards.notes: Use the Poughkeepsie approach for a daylight walk or ride across the pedestrian bridge; check weather and closing time before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A 1.28-mile elevated pedestrian bridge over the Hudson River with free regular-hours access.
cards.evidence_claim: Walkway Over the Hudson is a 1.28-mile elevated pedestrian bridge, and access is free during regular operating hours.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7:00 a.m. to sunset, weather permitting; confirm the day’s closing time and conditions before visiting.
